text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Ministers from the 18 APEC nations are expected to announce a major agreement on the mutual recognition of food standards next week in the Philippines, a decision which would mean a food product tested and certified in Australia would be recognised autmatically in other participating countries. The agreement is to cover labelling, export inspection, verification and certification of standards. Page 1.

A survey by research company www.consult reveals there has been a boom in new Internet Service Providers in the past six months, with one-third of the 308 companies having started business since May. According to Dot Communications' Alex von Kotze, it could be easier to set up as an ISP than it is to get a taxi licence, with small companies armed with less than A$10,000 and a home PC able to create an ISP. Page 1.

A full court ruling by the New South Wales Industrial Relations Commission yesterday that an executive share option plan operated by GIO Australia was unfair, clears the way for dismissed employees to claim a continuing entitlement to exercise their share options. The decision also affirms that employment contracts which allow executives to be terminated with limited notice are likely to be struck out under New South Wales laws. Page 3.

The latest shareholder notice reveals the Myer family was among several institutions who diluted their shareholding in Coles Myer last month as chairman Nobby Clark negotiated a boardroom peace deal. Myer Family Custodians Pty Ltd sold 187,934 shares beteen September 27 and November 1. Page 23.

Feeling the impact of lower local consumer spending and import competition, Southcorp Holdings Ltd managing director Graeme Kraehe said yesterday the group is looking to reposition its domestic appliance business and is seeking a joint venture or an alliace with a global appliance company to help it weather the next building downturn. Page 23.

Despite carrying a A$30 million debt into 1996-97, Mount Edon Gold Mines Ltd told yesterday's annual general meeting in Perth that the company remained committed to its goal of producing 150,000 tonnes of gold per annum within three years. Chairman Trevor Kennedy said production from the Tarmoola and Nevoria mines near Leonora in Western Australia was scheduled to exceed 100,000 ounces in a year for the first time in 1996-97. Page 24.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Productivity Commission is seeking Federal Cabinet approval to conduct an investigation into restrictive work practices in the black coal and stevedoring industries. With its productivity lagging behind the world's best producers, especially the Unitd States, the Productivity Commission would identify restrictive practices in the black coal industry, quantify their cost and consider the barriers to their removal. Page 23.

Sunbeam chairman and celebrity downsizer Al Dunlap announced yesterday he would sack 6000 of the US appliance maker's 12,000 workers, scrap 4350 of its 5000 product lines and close 39 of its 53 offices and factories in 16 States. Dunlap said the moves wold save Sunbeam US$225 million a year and double sales to US$2.4 billion over the next three years. Page 23.

Fearing Coles Myer Ltd shareholders might not have an opportunity to vote for him at all if next Tuesday's annual meeting proceeds as outlined, board candidate Peter Willcocks yesterday warned that he was considering legal action against Coles Myer to ensure the method of voting at the meeting does not discriminate against his candidacy. Page 23.

Although Metway Bank Ltd shareholders yesterday approved the mechanics of the A$19 billion merger with Suncorp and the Queensland Industry Development Corp, Metway chairman Frank Haly told shareholders they would need to approve a possible corporate name change, an increase in directors' fees and a performance incentive package involving the issue of shares or options to the chief executive officer. Page 25.

Because of the New South Wales Government's decision to scale back logging quotas to between 50 and 65 per cent of their June 1995 levels, Boral Ltd is expected to cut the number of its timber operations on the New South Wales north coast from 23 to as few as seven, with the sawmills at Mt George not expected to reopen after the industry's traditional Christmas break. Page 25.

According to a study funded by the Australian Research Council and the Chamber of Minerals and Energy in Western Australia, the wholesale, retailing and entertainment industries benefit the most from large capital investment in mining and mineral processing, with the A$3.6 billion in a typical year invested in construction of mining projects in Western Australia creating about 39,000 temporary jobs. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Despite accusations by former Queensland Premier Wayne Goss of a secret deal between the State Government and Metway Bank, Metway shareholders yesterday voted unanimously to approve a A$20 billion merger with the Queensland Government-owned Suncorp and Quensland Industry Development Corp. Page 25.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission is taking legal action on behalf of the owners of a Gold Coast service station, claiming that oil giant Shell lied to a franchisee and used its market power to force the franchisee to sell for a massive loss. The service station owners claim they were promised a further five-year extension by a Shell employee when they bought the franchisee rights for a one-plus-five-year tenure in 1993. Page 25.

After buying a slice of high-tech group Intag International ahead of a A$15 million sharemarket raising in 1994, investors James Packer, Rodney Adler and Andrew Kroger are hoping a move by Middle East company Middle East Nominees to raise its 14.39 per cet stake to the takeover threshold of 19.9 per cent will bring them some good fortune. Page 25.

Despite yesterday's release of figures from the Westpac-Melbourne Institute of consumer sentiment which showed an 8.3 per cent leap in consumer confidence ahead of the vital Christmas retailing period, Woolworths chief executive Reg Clairs played down the significance of the figures, saying they were nothing to get too excited about. Westfield executive chairman Frank Lowy also said the shopping centre group's retailers were still finding it tough. Page 25.

AWA chairman John Iliffe told yesterday's annual general meeting in Sydney that the company was still confident of achieving its full-year forecasts despite not meeting its first-quarter budget. Keno contracts secured in Nevada and the Philippines will help AWA's gaming, wagering, servicing and distributions businesses achieve their forecasts for the full year. Page 27.

Although Southcorp Holdings will depend on stronger growth from its wine and packaging division to offset weaker profits from the troubled appliance sector, chief executive Graham Kraehe told a Securities Institute of Australia lunch yesterday that an expected upturn in the housing construction industry from June 1997 would provide a solid base for growth in the company's whitegoods business. Page 27.
THE AGE

Attending the Screen Producers Association conference in Melbourne yesterday, WIN regional television network owner and chairman, Bruce Gordon, called for the abolition of cross-media ownership laws so he could buy local newspapers and radio stations in WN Television's broadcast areas. Page B1.

Set to be listed on the sharemarket on December 2, the Brisbane-based mega-bank proposal was approved yesterday by Metway Bank shareholders. The merger of Metway, Queensland Government-owned Suncorp and Queensland Industry Development Corp will see the Qeensland Government issued with 297.8 million shares - a 71 per cent holding. Page B1.

Following falls in interest rates, the Westpac/Melbourne Institute index of consumer sentiment rose 8.5 per cent in November to hit a five-month high. Westpac general manager, economics, Bill Evans, said the response was "remarkably strong" and there is ow a net balance of respondents expecting good economic conditions. Page B1.

Informing a Securities Institute of Australia lunch yesterday that cost reduction, overseas expansion and divestment of non-core assets would remain his main focus, Southcorp Holdings chief executive Graham Kraehe forecast improved profits for the diversiied group this financial year, based on stronger growth from its wine and packaging divisions. Page B3.

The Australian Shareholders Association yesterday served Coles Myer with a list of 62 questions that might also be asked at next Tuesday's annual meeting in Sydney, including queries over Coles' profit slide, the decline and fall of its World 4 Kids toy sore chain, management changes, transactions between the retailer and directors and the events surrounding the Yannon transaction. Page B3.

Forrestania Gold NL and Capricorn Resources have made a promising nickel strike in the lake Johnston region of Western Australia, with the companies reporting the return of a 6.7-metre intersection, grading 3.61 per cent nickel, from a depth of 193.3 metrs from one hole. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
